title: When sandwiches are not so simple
titleChinese: 当三明治变得不再简单
paragraphs: For many of us, sandwiches are something simple. Something we can take to work or school to avoid having to cook lunch, something we can buy quickly and cheaply. For many of us, we don't even need to stop working to eat them. Sandwiches could possibly be the ultimate convenience food.

But now it seems people are realising that the humble sandwich can be so much more. There's nothing convenient about waiting an hour and paying five times the price of a supermarket sarnie, but that's exactly what customers at one London sandwich shop have been doing. What is it that makes people so keen to get their hands on these £12 sandwiches?

Firstly, it's the ingredients. As baking has become more popular, good quality bread is both available and expected. The brains behind many of these gourmet sandwich shops are often people who have worked in the kitchens of top, Michelin-starred restaurants. This means that they bring a fine-dining attitude to their sandwiches, sourcing the best and freshest ingredients, combining them in new and creative ways. Secondly, it's the size. Max Halley, owner of a similar sandwich shop, boasts that the sandwiches his shop makes are twice the size of most burgers.

Finally, having sandwiches that look both huge and delicious is perfect for social media. While they may be more expensive than supermarket sandwiches, they are far more accessible than many other dining options. Being enticing, affordable, and trendy is an almost guaranteed way to attract attention online and bring crowds to the shops' doors. That's what's leading some to spend most of their lunch hour queueing up for a bite.

And why not? They might be a bit too expensive to have every day, but taking time away from your desk to eat something that has been thoughtfully prepared from fresh, high-quality ingredients isn't a bad thing. It could be a good alternative to munching on industrially-produced supermarket sandwiches at your desk while staring at a spreadsheet.

vocabulary.entry: **ultimate** /ˈʌltɪmət/ adj. 终极的，极端的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The ultimate goal of the project is to reduce pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的最终目标是减少污染。

vocabulary.entry: **convenience food** /kənˈviːniəns fuːd/ n. 方便食品，速食（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Convenience food is popular among busy people.
vocabulary.translation: 方便食品在忙碌的人群中很受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: **humble** /ˈhʌmbl/ adj. 谦卑的，不起眼的
vocabulary.example: She comes from a humble background.
vocabulary.translation: 她出身卑微。

vocabulary.entry: **sarnie** /ˈsɑːni/ n. 三明治（英式口语）
vocabulary.example: I'll just grab a sarnie for lunch.
vocabulary.translation: 我午饭就随便吃个三明治。

vocabulary.entry: **keen** /kiːn/ adj. 热衷的，渴望的
vocabulary.example: She was keen to get started on the project.
vocabulary.translation: 她渴望开始这个项目。

vocabulary.entry: **get one's hands on** /ˌɡet wʌnz ˈhændz ɒn/ phr. 得到，获得（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I'd love to get my hands on a copy of that book.
vocabulary.translation: 我很想得到那本书的副本。

vocabulary.entry: **ingredient** /ɪnˈɡriːdiənt/ n. 成分，原料
vocabulary.example: The list of ingredients includes flour, sugar, and eggs.
vocabulary.translation: 成分列表包括面粉、糖和鸡蛋。

vocabulary.entry: **baking** /ˈbeɪkɪŋ/ n. 烘焙，烤制
vocabulary.example: Baking is a relaxing hobby for many people.
vocabulary.translation: 烘焙对许多人来说是一种放松的爱好。

vocabulary.entry: **gourmet** /ˈɡʊəmeɪ/ n. 美食家；adj. 美食的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The restaurant serves gourmet food at high prices.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅以高价提供美食。

vocabulary.entry: **Michelin-starred** /ˈmɪʃəlɪn stɑːd/ adj. 米其林星级的（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The chef runs a Michelin-starred restaurant in Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 这位厨师在巴黎经营一家米其林星级餐厅。

vocabulary.entry: **fine-dining** /ˌfaɪn ˈdaɪnɪŋ/ n. 精致餐饮，高级餐厅用餐（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Fine-dining restaurants focus on high-quality ingredients and presentation.
vocabulary.translation: 精致餐饮餐厅注重高品质的食材和摆盘。

vocabulary.entry: **source** /sɔːs/ v. 获得（原材料）， sourcing（书面语）
vocabulary.example: We source our ingredients from local farmers.
vocabulary.translation: 我们从当地农民那里采购食材。

vocabulary.entry: **boast** /bəʊst/ v. 夸口，自夸（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He boasts that he can speak six languages.
vocabulary.translation: 他夸口说他会说六种语言。

vocabulary.entry: **burger** /ˈbɜːɡə(r)/ n. 汉堡包
vocabulary.example: I'll have a cheeseburger and fries.
vocabulary.translation: 我要一个芝士汉堡和薯条。

vocabulary.entry: **accessible** /əkˈsesəbl/ adj. 可获得的，易接近的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The website is accessible to all users.
vocabulary.translation: 所有用户都可以访问该网站。

vocabulary.entry: **dining option** /ˈdaɪnɪŋ ˌɒpʃn/ n. 用餐选择（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The city has many dining options for vegetarians.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市为素食者提供了许多用餐选择。

vocabulary.entry: **enticing** /ɪnˈtaɪsɪŋ/ adj. 诱人的，有吸引力的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The shop window displayed an enticing array of cakes.
vocabulary.translation: 商店橱窗里陈列着一排诱人的蛋糕。

vocabulary.entry: **affordable** /əˈfɔːdəbl/ adj. 负担得起的，价格合理的
vocabulary.example: The hotel offers affordable accommodation for families.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店为家庭提供价格合理的住宿。

vocabulary.entry: **trendy** /ˈtrendi/ adj. 时髦的，流行的（口语）
vocabulary.example: This area has become very trendy among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区在年轻人中变得非常时髦。

vocabulary.entry: **queue up** /ˌkjuː ˈʌp/ phr. v. 排队等候（英式）
vocabulary.example: People queued up to buy tickets for the concert.
vocabulary.translation: 人们排队等候购买音乐会门票。

vocabulary.entry: **bite** /baɪt/ n. 一小口食物（口语）
vocabulary.example: I'm hungry – let's grab a bite to eat.
vocabulary.translation: 我饿了——我们吃点东西吧。

vocabulary.entry: **thoughtfully** /ˈθɔːtfəli/ adv. 深思熟虑地，精心地（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The meal was thoughtfully prepared by the chef.
vocabulary.translation: 这顿饭是厨师精心准备的。

vocabulary.entry: **alternative** /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ n. 可供选择的事物（书面语）
vocabulary.example: We have no alternative but to wait.
vocabulary.translation: 我们别无选择，只能等待。

vocabulary.entry: **munch** /mʌntʃ/ v. 大声咀嚼，用力嚼（口语）
vocabulary.example: He was munching on an apple.
vocabulary.translation: 他正在大声嚼着一个苹果。

vocabulary.entry: **industrially-produced** /ɪnˈdʌstriəli prəˈdjuːst/ adj. 工业化生产的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Industrially-produced food often contains additives.
vocabulary.translation: 工业化生产的食品通常含有添加剂。

vocabulary.entry: **spreadsheet** /ˈspredʃiːt/ n. 电子表格
vocabulary.example: She spends hours each day working on spreadsheets.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天花数小时处理电子表格。

sentences.english: But now it seems people are realising that the humble sandwich can be so much more.
sentences.chinese: 但现在，人们似乎意识到，不起眼的三明治可以远不止如此。

sentences.english: There's nothing convenient about waiting an hour and paying five times the price of a supermarket sarnie, but that's exactly what customers at one London sandwich shop have been doing.
sentences.chinese: 等待一个小时并支付超市三明治五倍的价格，可一点也不方便，但这正是一家伦敦三明治店的顾客们一直在做的事情。

sentences.english: What is it that makes people so keen to get their hands on these £12 sandwiches?
sentences.chinese: 是什么让人们如此渴望得到这些12英镑的三明治呢？

sentences.english: Firstly, it's the ingredients.
sentences.chinese: 首先是食材。

sentences.chinese: 随着烘焙变得越来越流行，人们期待买到优质面包。

sentences.chinese: 一家类似三明治店的老板马克斯·哈利夸口说，他店里制作的三明治是大多数汉堡的两倍大。

sentences.chinese: 最后，拥有既巨大又美味的三明治非常适合社交媒体。

sentences.english: While they may be more expensive than supermarket sandwiches, they are far more accessible than many other dining options.
sentences.chinese: 虽然它们可能比超市三明治更贵，但比许多其他餐饮选择要容易获得得多。

sentences.chinese: 诱人、价格合理且时尚，几乎是吸引网络关注、让人们涌向店门的保证。

sentences.chinese: 这就是为什么有些人会把大部分午休时间花在排队等待一口美味上。

sentences.english: And why not?
sentences.chinese: 为什么不呢？

sentences.english: They might be a bit too expensive to have every day, but taking time away from your desk to eat something that has been thoughtfully prepared from fresh, high-quality ingredients isn't a bad thing.
sentences.chinese: 它们可能有点太贵，不适合每天吃，但离开办公桌，花点时间享用由新鲜、优质食材精心准备的食物，并不是坏事。

sentences.chinese: 与一边盯着电子表格一边在办公桌前大口咀嚼工业化生产的超市三明治相比，这可能是更好的选择。
